Transfer argument: Controls whether the destination hostname is resolved locally when using a SOCKS proxy.
false : The destination hostname is passed to the SOCKS proxy without local resolution. The SOCKS proxy resolves the hostname using its own DNS configuration. This allows connections to hostnames that are only resolvable from the proxy's network and allows hostname-based proxy rules, such as whitelists, to be applied. However, this can fail when using a SOCKS4-only proxy server, as SOCKS4 requires an IP address rather than a hostname.
true : The destination hostname is resolved locally before the connection is established. The SOCKS proxy receives the resulting IP address. This can be required when using a SOCKS4-only proxy server, but can fail if the hostname cannot be resolved locally or if the SOCKS proxy uses hostname-based rules, such as a whitelist.
Argument Scope and Precedence.
This argument applies to both SOCKS proxies: the source proxy and the target proxy, if configured.
If this argument is explicitly configured, it takes precedence over the configuration file and the corresponding environment variable PROXY_SOCKS_RESOLVE_HOSTNAME .

Processing argument: Specifies how to handle placeholder variable names that can be specified for replacement in the configuration file.
Examples: <Directory>${PLACEHOLDER_VARIABLE}</Directory>
true
only case-sensitive matches PLACEHOLDER_VARIABLE is resolved
false
PLACEHOLDER_VARIABLE , placeholder_variable etc. are resolved regardless of case

Processing argument: Specifies how to handle placeholder variables that can be specified in the configuration file for replacement if the placeholder cannot be replaced.
Examples: <Directory>${PLACEHOLDER_VARIABLE}</Directory>
true
If a placeholder variable cannot be replaced, the original value is returned: ${PLACEHOLDER_VARIABLE}
false
If a placeholder variable cannot be replaced, an empty value is returned.

Processing argument: Execute operations in parallel.
Affects all operations that support parallel execution, including:
Copy and Move - parallel file transfer
Remove - parallel deletion from Source
Note: This value is ignored or automatically set to the default value of 1 if parallel execution is not supported by the Source or Target provider.

Simulation argument for testing connectivity fault injection.
This simulates connectivity errors on the Source for testing and handling purposes.
A connectivity fault occurs after the specified interval in <seconds>.
<seconds> supports integer or float values, decimal separator: '.' or ',', e.g.:
1 - inject one connectivity fault after 1s
0.5;2.5;3 - inject connectivity faults 3 times (after 0.5s, then 2.5s, then 3s)

Simulation argument for testing connectivity fault injection.
Same format as source_sim_conn_faults , applied to the Target provider.

Simulation argument for testing connectivity fault injection.
Shorthand for Source AND Target connectivity faults, e.g.:
0.2;2 - inject faults for both providers at the same intervals
Serialized transfer result for File Transfer History.
